panels.description: Fraction of NeuronCores with utilization > 1%. Hardware-agnostic: the denominator is the total NeuronCore count reported by the daemon, so the thresholds (red < 25%, yellow < 75%, green ≥ 75%) work the same on trn1.2xlarge, trn1.32xlarge, and trn2.48xlarge fleets.
panels.title: Active Cores

panels.description: Percentile bands across all NeuronCores. The shaded area between p5 and p95 represents the spread of core utilization across the cluster.
panels.title: NeuronCore Utilization Distribution

panels.description: Average utilization per node — quickly identify imbalanced nodes.
panels.title: Utilization Per Node

panels.description: Device memory used per node, from the driver's ledger (all device_mem_* categories) — percentile bands across nodes.
panels.title: Device Memory Distribution

panels.description: Total device memory per node, from the driver's ledger (all device_mem_* categories).
panels.title: Total Device Memory Per Node (Stacked)

panels.description: Effective FLOPS percentile bands — measures actual compute throughput.
panels.title: Effective FLOPS Distribution

panels.description: FLOPS per node — identify compute imbalance.
panels.title: FLOPS Per Node

panels.description: Uncorrectable ECC errors per node — these indicate hardware degradation. Series stack repairable + unrepairable + sram (NOT corrected + uncorrected): the combined `mem_ecc_uncorrected` metric already includes the unrepairable portion, so stacking it on top of unrepairable would double-count fatal errors.
panels.title: Uncorrectable ECC Errors (repairable vs fatal)

panels.description: Core resets and failures per node.
panels.title: Core Resets

panels.description: End-to-end inference latency percentiles across active cores.
panels.title: Inference Latency (active cores)

panels.description: Host CPU usage percentiles across all nodes.
panels.title: Host CPU (min / avg / max across nodes)

panels.description: Memory utilization per node as percentage.
panels.title: Host Memory Utilization Per Node

panels.description: Swap usage per node. Any swap usage on an ML training node is a red flag — it means host memory is exhausted and performance will collapse.
panels.title: ⚠️ Swap Usage (any usage = memory pressure)

panels.description: Packet drops and failed RDMA work requests by node. Any sustained non-zero rate warrants per-interface investigation in the node dashboard.
panels.title: EFA Drops & RDMA Errors

panels.description: SRD reliability events over the Grafana rate interval. These counters are available only on Nitro v4 and newer; absence on older instances is expected.
panels.title: EFA SRD Reliability Events
